<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter outstaff run docs:cli`. Do not edit by hand. -->

The CLI is installed as `outstaff` with the alias `ost`.

```
ost [global options] <command> [options]
```

## Global options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--team <path|git-url>` | Team config to use: a file, a directory, or a git URL with an optional #ref. Defaults to OUTSTAFF_TEAM_FILE, OUTSTAFF_TEAM_REPO, then ./.outstaff/team.yaml or ./team.yaml. |
| `--json` | Print machine-readable JSON instead of text. |
| `-v, --version` | Print the version. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help. |

## ost validate

Check the team config for errors and warnings.

Loads the team file, checks it against the schema and cross-field rules, and lists every problem with its file, line and column. Warnings describe what will not work as written. Roles are checked against the stock catalog plus the team's ejected catalog (catalog.path); adapter names are not checked yet and are accepted as written, but the options of adapters this build ships are checked against that adapter's schema. The installed adapters check the identities they own (a Slack member id, a GitHub login or App bot login) and warn about malformed ones.

```
ost validate
```

Exit codes:

- 0: no errors (warnings are allowed)
- 1: the config has errors or could not be loaded

Examples:

```sh
ost validate
ost validate --team ../acme-team
ost validate --json
```

## ost team

Show the resolved team: humans, repos, people and integrations.

Prints the team as Outstaff sees it after defaults are applied, including each person's repo grants. Roles are checked against the stock catalog plus the team's ejected catalog; exits 1 if the config cannot be loaded or a role is unknown.

```
ost team
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the team was printed
- 1: the config could not be loaded or a role is not in the catalog

Examples:

```sh
ost team
ost team --json
```

## ost render

Render the working files of one person from the catalog.

Renders a person's skills, references, templates and process documents from the stock catalog (the installed @outstaff/catalog package) and the team's ejected catalog (catalog.path, relative to the team file; same-named roles and documents replace stock ones). Without --out it lists the files with their sizes; with --out it writes them below that directory, refusing a non-empty directory unless --force is given.

```
ost render <handle> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--out <dir>` | Write the files below this directory. |
| `--force` | Write into a non-empty --out directory. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the files were listed or written
- 1: the config or catalog could not be loaded, the person is unknown, rendering failed, or --out is not empty

Examples:

```sh
ost render sam
ost render sam --out ./work/sam
ost render sam --out ./work/sam --force
ost render sam --json
```

## ost eject

Copy stock catalog files into the team repository to customize them.

Copies stock catalog files into the ejected catalog (catalog.path next to the team file, .outstaff/catalog by default) and records, per file, the catalog version and hash they came from in .ejected.json, with a copy of the original under .base/. Ejected files win over stock files with the same path. Targets (one or more): a role name (all its files), process/<name>, references/<name>, templates/<name>, toolsets/<name>, or --all. Existing files are never overwritten unless --force is given. Use ost diff to see your changes and ost upgrade to merge a newer catalog.

```
ost eject [targets...] [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | Eject every stock role, process, reference, template and toolset. |
| `--force` | Overwrite files that already exist and reset their recorded base. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the files were copied
- 1: the team could not be loaded, the target is unknown, or a file exists and --force was not given

Examples:

```sh
ost eject developer
ost eject references/git
ost eject process/review-loop
ost eject --all
ost eject developer --force
```

## ost role new

Scaffold a custom role in the team's catalog.

Creates roles/<name>/role.yaml and SKILL.md in the ejected catalog (catalog.path next to the team file, .outstaff/catalog by default). Without --from, both files come from a minimal template with TODO placeholders; with --from <stock-role>, they are copies of that stock role with the name and title replaced. A custom role is not ejected: it is not recorded in .ejected.json, has no stock original, and ost upgrade leaves it alone. People can then use it as their role, and it can be extended by other roles. The name must be DNS-safe (lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters) and must not be a stock role; to customize a stock role use ost eject. An existing custom role is only replaced with --force.

```
ost role new <name> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--from <stock-role>` | Start from the text of this stock role. |
| `--title <title>` | Display title; defaults to the name in title case. |
| `--profile <profile>` | Permission profile: readonly, docs, code, infra. Defaults to docs, or the --from role's. |
| `--toolset <toolset>` | Tool bundle: base, code, infra. Defaults to base, or the --from role's. |
| `--force` | Replace a custom role that already exists. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the role was created
- 1: the team could not be loaded, the name is invalid or a stock role, the role exists and --force was not given, or an option is unknown

Examples:

```sh
ost role new auditor
ost role new qa --from reviewer --title "QA Engineer"
ost role new data-engineer --profile code --toolset code
```

## ost diff

Show how ejected catalog files differ from the stock version they came from.

Prints a unified diff of each ejected file against its recorded base (the copy stored under .base/ when it was ejected or last upgraded). Without a path it covers every ejected file; with one it covers that file or every file below that folder, for example roles/developer. Files without changes are not listed.

```
ost diff [path]
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the diff was printed (including when there are no changes)
- 1: the team could not be loaded or the path is not an ejected file

Examples:

```sh
ost diff
ost diff roles/developer
ost diff references/git.md
```

## ost upgrade

Merge a newer stock catalog into the ejected files.

For every ejected file, merges three ways: the recorded base, the installed stock file and your copy (git merge-file). Clean merges are written. Conflicts are written with standard conflict markers (client, base, stock) and listed; resolve them by editing the files. Recorded bases move to the new stock version and catalog.version in the team file is set to it. A file that no longer exists in the stock catalog is reported and left alone. A file you deleted is dropped from the record, so it follows stock again. The catalog is the one installed with this CLI; install the release you want first, then run this. --to must name that version.

```
ost upgrade [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--to <version>` | Expected target version; must equal the installed catalog version. |

Exit codes:

- 0: every file merged cleanly
- 1: the team could not be loaded, --to does not match the installed catalog, or there are conflicts

Examples:

```sh
ost upgrade
ost upgrade --to 1.2.0
```

## ost build

Validate the team and render every person strictly; for client image builds.

Checks the team config, loads the stock and ejected catalogs, rejects ejected files that still contain conflict markers from ost upgrade, and renders every person's working files. Fails on any error, so a broken customization stops the image build. Intended for a client Dockerfile: FROM ghcr.io/outstaff-ai/agent:<version>, COPY .outstaff /opt/outstaff/team/.outstaff, RUN ost build.

```
ost build
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the team validates and every person renders
- 1: any error

Examples:

```sh
ost build
ost build --team /opt/outstaff/team
```

## ost init

Scaffold .outstaff/team.yaml and .gitignore rules in the current directory.

Writes a commented team.yaml with the team name taken from the directory name, one placeholder human, and the repo from `git remote get-url origin` when there is one. No people are added; the file points to `ost hire`. Appends rules that keep secrets out of git to .gitignore when missing. Refuses to overwrite an existing team file unless --force is given. The global --team option is ignored.

```
ost init [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--separate-repo` | Write team.yaml at the repository root, for a repository that holds only the team config. The product repo then goes in `repos` as `kind: primary`. |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing team file. |

Exit codes:

- 0: files written
- 1: the team file already exists (use --force) or could not be written

Examples:

```sh
ost init
ost init --separate-repo
ost init --force
```

## ost setup

Prepare the credentials of one person or of the office.

Without --derive, writes `.outstaff/people/<handle>/.env.example` (or `.outstaff/office/.env.example`), which lists every secret the configured adapters need for that scope with where to get it, and prints a step-by-step guide per adapter. It never writes a real value. With --derive, reads the secrets already provided (files in the secrets directory first, then the environment), looks up the values that can be computed, such as GitHub App slug and installation id, the chat bot's user id and the tracker member id, and writes them as files into the secrets directory without printing them. If a `<app slug>.*.pem` was just downloaded to ~/Downloads, offers to move it there as the App's private key. Refuses to run unless the `.env` file and the secrets directory are ignored by git.

```
ost setup <handle|office> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--out <dir>` | Project directory to write `.outstaff/...` into. Defaults to the current directory. |
| `--derive` | Fill derivable secrets from the ones already provided instead of writing the template. |
| `--secrets-dir <dir>` | Directory of secret files, for the layout hint and for --derive. Defaults to OUTSTAFF_SECRETS_DIR, then ./secrets. |
| `--yes` | Do not ask before moving a downloaded private key. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the template was written, or values were derived
- 1: the team could not be loaded, the person is unknown, or the git ignore rules are missing

Examples:

```sh
ost setup sam
ost setup office --out .
ost setup sam --derive --secrets-dir ./secrets
ost setup sam --derive --yes --json
```

## ost workflow explain

Show which workflow rules an event triggers, and why.

Runs the team's workflow (its preset and rule overrides) against one event and a static snapshot of the world, and prints for every rule whether it matched, why, and what it would do. Nothing is applied. The event is JSON with a type, an optional subject, actor and data; the snapshot (--state) is JSON with tickets, prs, links and roles, and defaults to an empty world, in which most rules report that no ticket is linked.

```
ost workflow explain <event-json> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--state <json>` | World snapshot as JSON: {"tickets": {"ACME-1": {"status": "review"}}, "prs": [], "links": {"10": "ACME-1"}, "roles": {}}. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the event was explained (whether or not any rule matched)
- 1: the team config could not be loaded, or the event or state is malformed

Examples:

```sh
ost workflow explain '{"type":"ticket.assigned","subject":{"ticket":"ACME-1"},"actor":{"kind":"human","id":"dana"}}' --state '{"tickets":{"ACME-1":{"status":"ready","assignee":{"id":"sam","kind":"agent"}}}}'
```

## ost git-credential

Git credential helper: gives git a short-lived token for one repository.

Speaks git's credential helper protocol on standard input and output. For `get` it finds the team repository git is talking to, checks the person's grant on it and prints a short-lived token scoped to that repository and grant. `store` and `erase` do nothing, so no token is kept anywhere. Agents set it up per clone (credential.helper); you rarely run it by hand.

```
ost git-credential <operation>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: done; for `get` the answer is on standard output, empty when the request is not for a repository the person has a grant on
- 1: the operation is unknown or the token could not be issued

Examples:

```sh
git config credential.helper '!ost git-credential'
printf 'protocol=https\nhost=github.com\npath=acme-example/shop.git\n' | ost git-credential get
```

## ost ticket show

Show a ticket with its description and comments.

Shows a ticket: title, status, assignee, labels, description and its comments, with the ticket URL.

```
ost ticket show <key>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket show ACME-12
ost ticket show ACME-12 --json
```

## ost ticket comment

Add a comment to a ticket.

Adds a comment to a ticket and returns the link to it.

```
ost ticket comment <key> <body>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket comment ACME-12 "Pull request is up for review."
ost ticket comment ACME-12 "Pull request is up for review." --json
```

## ost ticket move

Move a ticket to another status.

Moves a ticket to a canonical status (backlog, ready, active, review, blocked, done, canceled). The tracker's own status names are mapped by the team's workflow settings.

```
ost ticket move <key> <to>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket move ACME-12 review
ost ticket move ACME-12 review --json
```

## ost ticket assign

Assign a ticket to a member, to yourself or to nobody.

Assigns a ticket. "to" is a tracker member (username, name or id), "me" for yourself, or "none" to unassign.

```
ost ticket assign <key> <to>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket assign ACME-12 me
ost ticket assign ACME-12 none
ost ticket assign ACME-12 me --json
```

## ost doc search

Search the knowledge base.

Searches documents by text and lists the matches with their URLs.

```
ost doc search <query> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--limit <limit>` | Maximum number of results. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost doc search "checkout flow"
ost doc search "checkout flow" --json
```

## ost doc show

Show a document and its comments.

Shows a document's text and its comment threads, with ids you can reply to or resolve.

```
ost doc show <id>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost doc show specs/checkout.md
ost doc show specs/checkout.md --json
```

## ost doc create

Create a document.

Creates a new document. It never overwrites: an existing path is a conflict.

```
ost doc create <path> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--title <title>` | Document title. |
| `--body <body>` | Document text, Markdown. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost doc create specs/checkout.md --title "Checkout" --body "# Checkout"
ost doc create specs/checkout.md --title "Checkout" --body "# Checkout" --json
```

## ost doc reply

Reply to a comment on a document.

Replies to a comment thread on a document.

```
ost doc reply <doc> <commentId> <body>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost doc reply specs/checkout.md c-3 "Done, see the new section."
ost doc reply specs/checkout.md c-3 "Done, see the new section." --json
```

## ost doc resolve

Resolve a comment thread on a document.

Marks a comment thread on a document as resolved.

```

```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:


## ost pr status

Show a pull request's state, checks and open review threads.

Shows a pull request: state, mergeability, checks and how many review threads are still open, with URLs.

```
ost pr status <repo> <number>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost pr status shop 42
ost pr status shop 42 --json
```

## ost pr threads

List the review threads of a pull request.

Lists the review threads of a pull request with their ids, locations, comments and URLs. Open threads only unless all is set.

```
ost pr threads <repo> <number> [options]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | Include resolved threads. |

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost pr threads shop 42
ost pr threads shop 42 --all
ost pr threads shop 42 --json
```

## ost pr resolve

Resolve a review thread whose last comment is yours.

Resolves a review thread after you have replied. It refuses when the last comment in the thread is not yours; the reviewer resolves those.

```
ost pr resolve <repo> <number> <thread>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost pr resolve shop 42 PRT_abc123
ost pr resolve shop 42 PRT_abc123 --json
```

## ost me

Show who you are on this team.

Shows your handle, role, repository grants and which integrations this team has connected.

```
ost me
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost me
ost me --json
```

## ost ask

Ask a teammate, or anyone with a role, a question through the office.

Asks a person of the team by handle, or a role (the least busy person with it answers; your own role means a peer). The office routes it; the answer may come later, as a new message in your work item. A role nobody has gets an explicit reply: ask a human.

```
ost ask <to> <question>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost ask mira "Should the cart survive a deploy?"
ost ask architect "Should the cart survive a deploy?"
ost ask mira "Should the cart survive a deploy?" --json
```

## ost answer

Answer a question a teammate asked you.

Answers a question that the office gave you as a work item. The asker continues their work with your answer. Only the person who was asked can answer, once.

```
ost answer <question> <answer>
```

Exit codes:

- 0: the verb succeeded
- 1: the input was invalid, the team or a port could not be reached, or the verb refused

Examples:

```sh
ost answer 01J9X "Use the fast queue; orders must not wait on mail."
ost answer 01J9X "Use the fast queue; orders must not wait on mail." --json
```
